plainEnglish.text: Authorizes the Burlingame Elementary School District to issue up to $100 million in bonds for school facility projects listed in the measure.
plainEnglish.excerpt: The Board of Trustees of the Burlingame Elementary School District (District) proposes this Measure, which would authorize the District to issue bonds in a principal amount not to exceed $100 million.

yes.text: A yes vote would authorize the District to issue bonds of up to $100 million for the purposes listed in the Bond Project List.

no.text: A no vote would prevent the District from issuing the bonds.

argAgainst.text: The argument against says voters already approved school bonds in 2012 and 2016 and opposes taking on more debt to update classrooms again.

argFor.text: The argument in favor says Belmont's 75-year-old Barrett Community Center has leaking roofs and failing systems and does not meet current safety and accessibility standards, and the measure would replace it with a new community center with emergency capacity.

plainEnglish.text: Amends Brisbane's Business License Tax by replacing the current tiered rates with a single gross receipts formula, deleting some special rate categories and exemptions, and updating definitions. It is a general tax for City services.
plainEnglish.excerpt: If approved by the voters, Measure X would amend the Business License Tax codified at Title 5, Division I of the Brisbane Municipal Code by replacing the current tiered rate structure with a single gross receipts formula, deleting some specialized categories of tax rates and exemptions while retaining others, and updating relevant definitions.

yes.text: A yes vote is a vote in favor of the measure, which would replace the current business license tax rates with a single gross receipts formula.
yes.excerpt: A “Yes” vote is a vote in favor of the Measure.

no.text: A no vote is a vote against the measure; the current tax structure would remain in place.
no.excerpt: A “No” vote is a vote against the Measure. If the Measure is not approved, the current tax structure will remain in place.

fiscal.text: Businesses with gross receipts of $25,000 or less would pay $50; businesses with more would pay $50 plus $1.00 for every $1,000 of gross receipts above $25,000. The City estimates about $1,000,000 in additional annual revenue.
fiscal.excerpt: A business with gross receipts of $25,000 or less would pay a tax of $50. A business with more than $25,000 in gross receipts would pay $50 plus $1.00 for every $1,000 in gross receipts above $25,000.

argFor.text: The argument in favor says the measure is a reasonable update so businesses contribute their fair share toward City services, raising fees not adjusted since 1983 and simplifying the rate structure.
argFor.excerpt: This measure is a reasonable update to Brisbane's Business License Tax to ensure that businesses contribute their fair share toward City Services.
argFor.location: Argument in favor (page 3 of PDF), paragraph 1

supporters.text: Coleen Mackin, Mayor; Madison Davis, Mayor Pro Tem; Frank Kern, Councilmember; Cliff Lentz, Councilmember; Terry O'Connell, Councilmember

plainEnglish.text: Raises Burlingame's hotel tax (Transient Occupancy Tax), paid by guests staying less than 30 days, from 12% to 15%. It is a general tax for City purposes.
plainEnglish.excerpt: Measure D would amend Chapter 4.09.025, “Tax Rate,” of Chapter 4.09 of Title 4 of the Burlingame Municipal Code, to increase Burlingame’s Transient Occupancy Tax rate by three percentage points, from 12% to 15%.

yes.text: A yes vote would raise the Transient Occupancy Tax rate from 12% to 15%.
yes.excerpt: A “Yes” vote would approve amending the Transient Occupancy Tax rate from 12% to 15%.

no.text: A no vote would reject the measure and keep the current 12% tax rate.
no.excerpt: A “No” vote would reject the measure and keep the current 12% tax rate.

fiscal.text: Raises the hotel tax rate from 12% to 15%, estimated to bring in an additional $5.7 million a year; the tax would stay in place until changed or repealed by voters.
fiscal.excerpt: If adopted, Measure D would generate an estimated additional $5.7 million annually, based on existing occupancy rates, room rates, and total number of hotel rooms in Burlingame.

argFor.text: The argument in favor says the measure makes hotel guests help pay for the City services they use, so local homeowners and residents do not bear the full cost.
argFor.excerpt: Voting YES on Measure __ ensures that hotel guests help fund the services they use, so local homeowners and residents don’t bear the full cost.

argAgainst.text: The argument against says the tax increase would discourage visitors and that the City Council should fund streets, sidewalks and emergency services in its regular budget.
